papers.abstract_en: BACKGROUND: The clinical significance and biological roles of PSMB7 in lung adenocarcinoma (LUAD) remain incompletely understood. This study aimed to comprehensively characterize PSMB7 expression, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, immune associations, and in vitro functions in LUAD. METHODS: PSMB7 expression, clinicopathological associations, prognostic value, epigenetic regulation, co-expression networks, functional pathways, and relationships with the tumor immune microenvironment were systematically evaluated across multiple datasets. External validation was performed in the GSE31210 cohort. Prognostic nomogram performance was additionally evaluated using Harrell's concordance index (C-index) and time-dependent decision curve analysis (DCA). In vitro experiments, including Western blotting, CCK-8 assays, and flow cytometry, were conducted to assess the effects of PSMB7 on cell proliferation and irradiation-induced apoptosis in LUAD cell lines. RESULTS: PSMB7 was significantly upregulated in LUAD and was associated with advanced pathological T and N stages and overall clinical stage. ROC analysis indicated that PSMB7 showed potential discriminatory ability between LUAD and normal lung tissues. High PSMB7 expression independently predicted unfavorable outcomes across multiple prognostic endpoints. Nomogram evaluation using calibration, C-index, and DCA provided complementary evidence for prognostic performance. PSMB7 hypomethylation was associated with poorer survival. PSMB7 expression was positively correlated with DNA mismatch repair genes, RNA modification regulators, and malignant tumor phenotypes. GSEA showed significant enrichment of oncogenic, cell-cycle, metabolic, DNA-repair, and stress-response pathways. In addition, PSMB7 expression was strongly associated with immune scores, immune-cell infiltration, and the expression of immune modulators, MHC molecules, chemokines, and chemokine receptors in LUAD. In vitro, PSMB7 knockdown suppressed cell proliferation and enhanced irradiation-induced apoptosis, whereas PSMB7 overexpression promoted proliferation and reduced apoptosis after irradiation. CONCLUSION: PSMB7 is a candidate independent prognostic biomarker in LUAD and is associated with malignant progression, immune microenvironment features, and cellular responses to irradiation consistent with a potential role in radioresistance. These findings support PSMB7 as a potential therapeutic target in LUAD.

papers.abstract_en: To investigate the biological functions of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma and further elucidate its underlying regulatory mechanisms. The Cancer Genome Atlas clinical cohorts, single-cell sequencing, Kaplan-Meier survival analysis, immunohistochemistry, qRT-PCR, and Western blot were performed to assess the expression and prognostic value of PPP1R14B in lung adenocarcinoma. Then, PPP1R14B-silenced A549 cells and PPP1R14B-overexpressing H1650 cells were constructed. Colony formation, CCK-8, EdU assay, flow cytometry, scratch, and Transwell chamber assays were utilized to evaluate cell proliferation, apoptosis, migration, invasion, and paclitaxel (PTX) resistance. To elucidate the molecular mechanism of PPP1R14B, transcriptome sequencing (RNA-seq) and co-immunoprecipitation assays were conducted. Additionally, a xenograft tumor mouse model was established to explore the in vivo role of PPP1R14B. PPP1R14B exhibited high expression in lung adenocarcinoma and correlated with an unfavorable prognosis. Silencing of PPP1R14B markedly suppressed the proliferation, migration, and invasion of A549 cells, while concurrently promoting apoptosis and sensitizing cells to PTX. Nevertheless, overexpression of PPP1R14B in H1650 cells displayed an opposite trend. PPP1R14B directly interacted with ARPC1A and promoted its expression. Overexpression of ARPC1A reversed the inhibitory effects of PPP1R14B silencing on the malignant biological behaviors of A549 cells. In vivo, silencing of PPP1R14B repressed tumor growth, as evidenced by smaller tumor volume, lower tumor weight, fewer Ki67-positive cells, and more TUNEL-positive cells. PPP1R14B directly binds ARPC1A and increases its expression to facilitate lung adenocarcinoma tumorigenesis and PTX resistance.

papers.abstract_en: Non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC) cells frequently depend on Nrf2/ARE-driven antioxidant programs to maintain redox balance and evade apoptosis. This study investigated whether sinensetin, a naturally occurring polymethoxylated flavone, reduces NSCLC cell survival by interfering with this cytoprotective pathway. A549 and H1299 NSCLC cells and normal BEAS-2B bronchial epithelial cells were exposed to sinensetin. Cell viability was measured by MTT assay, apoptosis was quantified by Annexin V-FITC/PI flow cytometry, and pathway- and apoptosis-related proteins were analyzed by western blotting. Nrf2 distribution was evaluated by nuclear/cytoplasmic fractionation, ARE-dependent transcription was assessed using a dual-luciferase reporter system, and Nrf2 was silenced by shRNA. Intracellular ROS was measured by DCFH-DA, antioxidant rescue was assessed with N-acetyl-l-cysteine (NAC), Nrf2/ARE-related proteins were examined in BEAS-2B cells, and Nrf2 overexpression was used as a rescue approach in A549 cells. Sinensetin inhibited NSCLC cell growth, increased apoptosis, reduced total and nuclear Nrf2, decreased ARE reporter activity, and downregulated HO-1 and NQO1. Sinensetin also increased intracellular ROS, whereas NAC partially reduced ROS accumulation, restored cell viability, and decreased apoptosis. BEAS-2B cells showed comparatively modest Nrf2/ARE pathway changes. Nrf2 overexpression partially restored HO-1 and NQO1, reduced apoptotic signaling, and attenuated sinensetin-induced loss of viability and apoptosis. These results support a model in which sinensetin promotes oxidative stress-mediated apoptosis in NSCLC cells, at least in part, through suppression of Nrf2/ARE-dependent antioxidant defense.
